review_text: Excellent! The food was delicious and the service was incredibly fast! Highly recommended. The menu is very varied!

author: Carin Rudich
review_text:
Eyval is a must especially if you love
Persian food.
The restaurant is open and airy and is much bigger than you realize. There are three separate dining areas to it.
There were 3 of us and we definitely over ordered but wanted to try different dishes.
See the photos. We had some serious leftovers.
The cocktails are unique in flavor and easy to drink.
Our waiter was very sweet and thoroughly explained the dishes and guided us on what to order. The entire staff was very personable every time they came to the table, either to bring food or clear the table.
Unbelievable flavors in these well curated dishes!
Reservations required!!!

author: Kiariladyboss
review_text:
One of the most delicious Persian dinner and food in NYC. They are usually booked 2 weeks in advance but people cancel all the time so keep checking for a spot to become available.

The squash spread and the eggplant dish were out of this world🤯🤤
Loved the Persian cocktail too. Service was fast and staff very nice.

Spot super recommended!

author: Robyn Lewis
review_text: Excellent everything.  Really good food, nice wine, great service.  Loved the octopus and squash dip in particular.  I will be back and send others here.  I wish I could have tried the whole menu!  Just amazing.  Also loved the radish etc salad!

author: Aylin A
review_text: This Persian fusion gem never misses. Every visit delivers incredible quality, from their must-have kashke bademjoon to the perfectly seasoned koobideh. Their seasonal additions—like the new mahi and kabab torsh—bring a bold, sour-leaning flavor that’s just as unforgettable. Reservations can be tricky at prime hours, but the first-come, first-served bar seating is a lifesaver. If you want consistently exceptional Persian fusion, this is the place

author: Sara Kazemi
review_text:
I was visiting New York, and my friends had secured a reservation here weeks in advance — and I can see why! The vibes were immaculate — a perfect blend of modern and Persian aesthetics. The music, the staff, the atmosphere — everything was spot on.

We ordered the Barbare bread with masto moosir, the octopus kebab, the kashkeh bademjoon, and the kebab — every single dish was incredible. The flavors were authentic yet elevated, enhancing traditional Persian spices beautifully.

This was hands down one of the best Persian meals I’ve ever had outside of someone’s home. 10/10 — if you haven’t tried it yet, you need to. Absolutely amazing! I will deff be going back here when I come to New York again

author: Graham Parker
review_text:
Utterly outstanding. One of my best meals of 2025.

I was recommended to come here by my husband, who is a tad obsessed with it, and now I can see why! Nothing better than seeing a thriving spot take food, dishes, ingredients, service and buzz so seriously.

The menu is varied and full of surprises, and not all dishes will work for all the pallettes at the table, and that is what makes it fun. You share everything and try lots of culinary ideas and see what sticks!

author: Massimo
review_text:
We went to Eyval for dinner and found parking without much trouble. The place had a nice energy with a modern look and a comfortable crowd.

The kitchen was fast and the food was excellent. The ghorme sabzi had deep flavor and tender meat. The tahdig was golden and crisp, and the kabob was juicy and well seasoned with saffron rice and grilled tomatoes.

The servers, however, weren’t very attentive. Drinks sat empty for a while, and it took some effort to get their attention. For two people, the total was about $120, which felt fair for the quality.

Overall, Eyval delivers top Persian food and a great vibe, but the service could be more engaged to match the kitchen’s pace.

author: Isabella Grandic
review_text:
Maybe I got a bad apple, but this was some of the laziest, sloppiest service I’ve had… ever. Especially for a restaurant of this calibre. (Will elaborate)

The food was good. Some of it was not good. The beef short ribs tasted were filled with what tasted like canned beans. Lamb ribs, which everyone seems to holler about, were not for me?? I couldn’t eat more than 1. A combination of the texture + the overpowering sauce.

The bread is good but y’all it’s $6 bread. It should come with the dips. The yogurt dip was basic but good. The Brussels sprouts dip was good. Desserts were good!

Only thing I would order again is the Wagyu kebab situation. That was yummy

I think the play here is a lot a lot of dips. Maybe the fish / chicken is better than the red meat, it didn’t hit for me.

The drinks. The Saffron martini tasted purely like moonshine, I got exactly zero saffron. Their coffee based cocktail I didn’t love (tasted cheap?). The cucumber mint one was alright and the mezcal pepercorn one was good. Draft beer was super whatever.

However, our server was on a different planet, one where attention to detail doesn’t exist. She came up to us for the first time asking for dessert. I was like we’ll start with the meal first 😂. Ordered cocktails which took 30+ minutes to come. Then, when it came to ordering food, we asked for recs. She started just recommending something and then adding it to our bill. I had to stop her, ask her to please stop adding things to our list and let us choose lmao. “I will add one of those” should not be something the server says, unless it’s on the house! It took her 45+ minutes to return with a draft beer. When I asked for the dessert menu, she gave me the drink menu and returned 20 mins later asking what we wanted for dessert, to which I had to say, I don’t know because we didn’t have the menu! They also delivered the wrong bread and the wrong cocktail during our dinner

A lot of people have loved this place and I fully went in hoping to join the club, but unfortunately this meal and experience fell quite short for me.

author: Reza Nia
review_text:
We had been long waiting for the opportunity to try Eyval, and it turned out to be a delightful experience overall. The ambiance was warm and inviting, and the servers were incredibly friendly and attentive. The food was a mix of good and fantastic.

The lamb ribs were absolutely out of this world. Chenjeh was also fantastic. For both dishes, I would happily give them more than five stars if I could. Koobideh was good, on the upper side of good, I would rate it 4.5 stars. Ghormeh sabzi and tahdig were both below my expectations, I gave them 4 stars.

Overall, the restaurant experience was more of a 4.5 to 4, but I had to choose between 4 and 5 stars, it would definitely be 4. I will definitely return if it’s only for the lamb ribs!

author: Nima Azizpour
review_text:
Eyval is by far the best Persian restaurant I have ever been to. The food is absolutely fantastic—each dish feels like a true work of art. Chef Ali is not only an incredibly talented chef but also a wonderful human being and a true artist when it comes to creating unforgettable flavors.

The vibe of the restaurant is unmatched. Everyone who works there is so warm and kind—it feels like being welcomed into one big family where their only goal is to make every guest happy. The energy and atmosphere are just perfect.

This place deserves a Michelin star without question. Everything is made fresh the same day, and you can truly taste that freshness in every single bite.

If you’re looking for an unforgettable dining experience, Eyval is it.

author: Rebecca McCall
review_text:
Worth the wait! The drinks, the decor, WOW. Highly recommend the Brussels sprouts. The saffron cream sauce this sit in is TO DIE. ❤️💚

Friends were out of town, so I went alone anyway and didn’t regret it.

author: Ali Bakhsh
review_text: Contemporary Persian food with a lot of great menu options executed at a higher level. Overall I enjoyed my dining experience here, there wasn’t really a standout dish that blew me away.

author: James On Al
review_text:
I wish this place was good, but We couldn't find what we're looking for and Price that we paid absolutely does not match the quality we get from the food,

Some dishes tasted really but others tasted like nothing , flavorless or flat.

They did good job with adding spices to tahini and other sauces and dressings, but again not all dishes.....

Waiter was not able focus or answer our all questions , They were just rushing,  running....

Our experience was just okay, May be but may be can come back just for specific dishes hope they can keep their tastes good

author: Pamela A
review_text: This place is awesome! My family and I had the best meal. The menu is made for sharing. Every dish we ordered was the best I’ve had. The service was great. The team worked together seamlessly. We were not rushed. The dishes were brought out in a timely fashion. Our table was never devoid of food. The drinks were unique and delicious. The vibe was great!

author: Brittany Ng
review_text:
Eyval was nothing short of fantastic! This was my first time trying Persian food and I was truly amazed by every dish we tried. The flavor combinations were unique and delicious, with the perfect mix of sweet and savory. We tried both the komaj bread and barbari bread, which had perfect textures of soft and fluffy. The citrus date salad was super refreshing and light with deep flavors from the dressing and dates, which was the perfect appetizer. We decided to try the lamb ribs, octopus kabob, and kabob koobideh as our entrees. The meat for all dishes were amazingly tender and flavorful, with the ribs falling right off the bone and the octopus perfectly chewy. The star of the shows in these dishes however, was the tomato butter that was served on top of the basmati rice in the kabob koobideh! It was so savory without being salty and wish there was more on the plate. I recommend all of these to share!

The interior was simple but beautifully designed, creating a nice ambiance that takes you out of New York City.  As you walk further in, you’re able to view the kitchen where chefs are carefully crafting each dish.

The service was exceptional also! Our server was very attentive to our table, making sure dishes were cleared and plates were swapped out for an easy dining experience. I also mentioned it was my birthday and they served my dessert with candle, which was a very thoughtful gesture.

Overall, this place was the perfect birthday dinner and glad I ventured out to try new food here! We are already thinking about our next visit to try more of their menu as I’m sure every dish will not disappoint.

author: Anja A.
review_text:
This place is amazing! We went two times in a short period of time since we were thinking about their food and other dishes we haven't tried.
Some of the must tries are: Barbari Bread, Yellow French Bean Borani, Citrus Date & Cabbage Salad, Lamb Ribs, Grilled Scallops, Eggplant.

author: Cameron Weeks
review_text: Good Persian spot in East Williamsburg with tough to get reservations. The bread and dips/sauces were probably our favorite items but everything was delicious. The kebab plate was also more plentiful than we were expecting and tasty.

author: Debarati
review_text:
The food is SOOO good. This was supposed to be a stop during my trip but realized that our rehearsals for our NY performance clashed exactly will Eyval's opening hours. I was super sad so my husband decided to get me take out!! I am SO pleased. He got me photos of the food and the plating is so beautiful. I hope I get to visit NY again just so I can eat at Eyval again haha ..and perhaps next time in person! I got to try the lamb...I don't even know how they made it that good. I loved the dry pomegranates on top. The color is so beautiful too. Tried the salad & the roasted eggplant. Both very yummy. The cardamom chocolate cake was DIVINE!! 😍
Highly recommend!!!

author: Sue-Ann C
review_text:
Eyval wants to be taken seriously as a dining experience, but someone forgot to plan for New York in winter.

Let’s start with the absurd: there is nowhere to put a coat. No rack. No hooks. No designated space. Just guests awkwardly draping long winter coats over weak chair backs and laps like it’s a casual café in April. And if your coat is long, it’s now dragging on the wet floor from snow laden shoes in the dining room. I even asked the hostess (who asked the manager) where can I put my long coat and both had ZERO solutions; so, I ended up resting my faux fur coat on the edge of a planter off the ground. This is NYC— we are fashionable and winter isn’t a surprise! If you’re charging these prices and aiming for elevated dining, basic hospitality logistics matter.

Service didn’t help. While very polite, our waiter messed up the order, he missed an item then gave incorrect information so we ended up with three very hefty rice bowls which imbalanced the meal. They also delivered a slice of chocolate cake for my birthday with a candle with no fanfare… no song, no “happy birthday,” no joy; it literally felt like a plop on the table. The cake wasn’t even good - tasted like it absorbed the smells of the fridge (they professionally removed that from our bill - thank you).

And speaking of balance: serving a feta dip with no bread (and no proactive explanation or accompaniment) is just baffling. Dips require vehicles. This isn’t revolutionary dining—it’s basic sense.

The frustrating part is that the food itself has moments of brilliance. The flavors are thoughtful, layered, and crafted with care. Very rich. Which makes the execution issues even more glaring. Eyval isn’t missing the mark because of ambition—it’s falling short  because of avoidable oversights.

In a city overflowing with restaurants that understand both food and fundamentals, Eyval needs to decide what it wants to be: a memorable dining experience or a beautiful concept undone by preventable mistakes. Right now, it’s hovering uncomfortably in between—coat in hand.

It’s not worth the reservation scarcity.

author: Frank Garcia
review_text:
I was wowed by my experience at Ey-vál. This has been one of the best Persian food I have had, they certainly ey-vál which is a Farsi(Persian) word that adds positive emphasis to an idea. I’m surprised they are not in the Michelin guide but I’m sure they will make it sooner than later.

The service was top notch. Super friendly and professional, fairly fast, knowledgeable about the menu and attentive.

Ambiance was dark, enigmatic, hip, I liked it a lot.

The food, what we came for, was beyond delicious. We started with the Mast o Musir and I gotta admit I have had great ones before and thought it would be hard to beat, but this one goes to the top of the list now. So so creamy, with shallots cut at the perfect size and acidity balanced out.

I continued with a salad( can’t remember its name) and while this was not a truly Persian dish, I loved the modern approach and all the flavors they accomplished on this dish. It was my second favorite dish after the mast o musir.

The lamb ribs were a solid dish. The sauce had the perfect sweetness/acidity as well as spiciness and the barberry on top complemented so sell.

The two kabobs were nicely done but my favorite was the koobideh. This is a personal preference as I’m more into koodideh than steak kabob. I understand the chenjeh is more premium, but it is just my preference. All in all, the 2 kabobs were 5 out 5 stars.

Tahdig which is one of my favorite Persian dishes and a really simple dish, was perfection in a single bite. That sauce they had the rice on, it was spot on. They made it also so good looking. I loved it.

You can’t leave a Persian restaurant without having Persian ice cream. However, to be honest it didn’t do it for me. There were a few flaws : typical Persian ice cream sandwich is with crispy and thin waffles, this one was with a soggy bread, also the ice cream was not as creamy as it should be. The ice cream sandwich was subpar compared to the high quality of the food I had.

All in all, looking forward to my next time at Ey-vál. Please open a location in Miami :)

author: Taylor Shields
review_text: I’ve eaten here several times and really enjoy the friendly service. The food is good, it is clean and the price is generally what I’d expect. I like the way they wrap the burritos.

author: Porsha Wakefield
review_text: The customer service is amazing, the food is always fresh, and the establishment is very clean. My daughter and I absolutely enjoy going there! I love the chicken bowl because of the freshness of the chicken. The gentleman was very nice with accommodating my daughter’s dietary restrictions which I really appreciated! They’ve gained loyal customers for sure!

author: Alvin
review_text: This was my first time ordering food from this restaurant. I was pleasantly surprised. The food was delicious the service was quick and the price was good. I ordered the nachos with the Chipotle chicken and I will definitely be returning. The young man who served us was also very nice. 5 stars.

author: Olga Caro
review_text: Minu was amazing — so kind, professional, and welcoming. After a long day, she made us feel completely taken care of and served the most delicious food. Truly went above and beyond! Best Mexican food and feels so healthy!

author: Yessica Agramonte
review_text: Very nice environment and clean! The food looks and tastes great. Jabran provides excellent customer service with a friendly and welcoming vibe. Highly recommend Adobo Mexican Grill! Additional details about the mango sauces it’s amazing

author: mightymtzion
review_text: Had the corn shredded chicken tacos. Omg so good so satisfying. Juicy chicken tacos filled overstuffed not skimpy. The sauces paired brilliantly. Would have left pic but its all gone now😂

author: angee ruiz
review_text: The employees were really kind and welcoming! Way better flavors than Chipotle (yuck). The food really is fresh even the work station are cleared and wipe right away. The birria is freaking amazing The meat is juicy and melts in your mouth. The quesadilla is done in front of you, really tasty. The guac is a most have.

author: Nohelia V
review_text: The food was really enjoyable, even with the odd combination of choices we had put into it. We both got two proteins and two drinks and it still ended up not even breaking past $40. Wayyy better than Chipotle 🤣

author: Richard Burgos
review_text: This place rocks for tacos, burritos and more. So good. Can't wait to come back.

author: Jhesi Rivero
review_text: Great service. Great food always fresh and tastes great. I moved here a year ago and never started coming here until a few months ago. They’re open late and always delicious. I usually get the nachos or burrito

author: Chadsity Jady
review_text:
Stick to CHIPOTLE! the food is tasteless, the name of the restaurant does not match the authenticity of the food! I am of latin culture and this food taste nothing of "Mexican Grill" pls don't be fooled, the food isn't the worst but it's definitely not what I was expecting being that it's trying to copy chipotle!
I also expected Latinos to be in there cheffin it up due to the name of the restaurant but instead I was met by 2 (asian Indians) which one of them said he was the owner as I was trying to place my order with him, he was having a conversation with his cook in his native language which I had to stop and wait until he was done, so the service sucks and the food taste like school lunch that copied chipotle!

author: Emma Gubitz
review_text:
This place is absolutely incredible! Since it opened not too long ago, I’ve been here 4-5 times, and each visit just gets better. The quality and flavor keep improving, and it genuinely blows me away every time. Imagine Chipotle, but with tastier food, better prices, and way bigger portions—you really get so much for your money!

What truly sets this place apart, though, is the staff. They are unbelievably kind and go out of their way to make your experience special. On my last visit, one of the staff members noticed I was loading up on hot sauce and asked if I liked really spicy food. When I said yes, he smiled and said, “One sec.” A couple of minutes later, he came out with a free birria taco just for me to try because he knew I’d love the heat. That small gesture seriously made my day.

author: Sourav Panchal
review_text: It was a great experience for me and my family the food was so fresh and delicious and one more thing is the employee are good welcome and understanding about his food and everything service is so good

author: Heidi Nuss
review_text: Excellent! Cilantro lime rice and the honey Chipotle chicken were amazing together!

author: Joshly Villegas
review_text: Just ate here today with my family for my moms bday. All I gotta say great service and great food. The staff are wonderful and very nice. Am soo eating here again.

author: Jontee Samuels
review_text: I come here often & the employees are always so nice & the food never misses. The buy one get one on Uber eats comes in super clutch too! Try the honey chicken!

author: Vincent Arena
review_text: Birria tacos were amazing as was the honey chicken bowl - staff is super friendly and prices are way better than chipotle!

author: Haider X
review_text: My go to Halal Mexican food.  Portions are very filling.  Packaging and food is great.

author: Nori Velazquez
review_text: Excellent service,  thumbs up for Patel he was very helpful, patient with us . Excellent customer service on his behalf. The food was excellent. We had different dishes.  Steak birria tacos were excellent . The steak is so savory , the honey chipotle chicken on point.  We enjoyed our meals thank you so much Patel for the food recommendation .

author: Anne Smith
review_text: I loveeee the quesadillas here but this is some of the slowest service I’ve ever received. There are 5 guys wandering in and out of the kitchen but only one man moving at a snail’s pace to make food. They’re so friendly but PLEASE please could we move faster 😭

author: Riccardo
review_text:
Buzzy/noisey atmosphere at the entrance, good host and reception with drinks at the bar before table was ready. Waiters not really alert, they messed up with my order, still smiley at least.
The pizza is very good/authentic Italian, average price 20 dollars each, but the service is very slow(and I mean it). Can’t say I loved the dessert as I left most of the pancake. Will still be definitely back as the it’s probably best pizza in Brooklyn.

author: Kevin Shapiro
review_text: Kitchen cool Brooklyn vibe. Indoor and outside seating.  2 bars. The one we were at you could get food from, but every time you went back up for anything such as a drink or anything like that you had to stand on an enormously long line and wait quite a while, which wasn't great. The meatballs were very good, and the regular and Margherita pies were very tasty. Crust was soft, not crispy and thin.

author: Beyase Warton
review_text: My friend and I wanted to stop by a place to get something to eat before we went back home to the city and this was recommended to us! They make really good daiquiris and their pizza is delicious! The staff was nice and the whole vibe of the place "outside" was so cool!

author: William Kim
review_text: Really good neopolitan style pizza. The dough is so good. One of my favorites. Fresh ingredients. I got the Famous Original and Bee Sting. Both had a little spicy kick to it, nothing crazy. Honey on bee sting was perfect combo to spice and soppressata.

author: Andrew Schneider
review_text: Amazing pizza joint, perhaps the best I've had in Brooklyn. Dive atmosphere. Great wine list. Service from Lauren was amazing.

author: Pat Lisi
review_text:
Well I’ll start with saying I’ve never been so sure I was about to be robbed as I was when our cab driver took us into this industrial area which was pitch black as it was night time. When the car stopped and there was nothing around I was sure it was my time to go !! However the cab driver pointed to a red light over a small vestibule and said “that’s it”  was beyond relieved to know we were still gonna make it !!

As we had no reso we had to wait two and a half hours for a table as the place was packed.

The pizzaiolos were very friendly and talked to us about everything pizza and more.

I asked some questions about the oven as it didn’t look like any I ever saw live or when I shop for my own and then they explained it was basically home made on the spot and that’s just amazing and very cool .. especially because they’re churning out NYC’s best pizza.

Very vibey atmosphere , very friendly staff … incredible pizza. 🍕

10/10

author: R Juliza
review_text: Honorary mention to Luis who worked diligently and gracefully even when something wasn’t up to par Luis ensured to fix it right there and then no hesitation no attitude or mal intent. Such a kind soul made me feel like I was right where I belonged. Thanks Luis. S/o kitchen staff also food is yummmieeee

author: Rovik Robert
review_text: Very good pizza in a vibey Brooklyn space that has lots of character. Decent selections of beers and wine to pair as well.

author: Ti Na
review_text: Don’t judge a book by its cover. From the outside, you question if you’ve come to the right place but don’t let that fool you,the food is great!  Highly recommend a reservation. When you walk in, you’ll be greeted by the pizza oven and staff. Atmosphere is cozy, low light with candles on the table. We had a salad to start along with olives and meatballs. All were good and large enough to share. The pizza is Neapolitan style. Crust is very good, soft with the slightest crunch and char. Sauce is good and toppings of sausage and meatballs are flavorful. Staff were attentive and very nice. They’ll box up your left overs for you too.  Will return.

author: Tera Nakata
review_text: A solid, tasty pizza. Slightly pricey. Got the Waingro and Bee Sting. A bit out of my way to get here but would recommend if you're in the neighborhood.

author: Susy “REALTOR” Velazquez
review_text: Loved it! The atmosphere at Roberta’s is rustic and inviting, creating the perfect setting for a great meal. We tried four different pizzas, and each one was delicious. The flavors were well-balanced, the crust was perfect, and everything tasted fresh. Highly recommend for anyone looking for good pizza in Brooklyn!

author: stephen shustock
review_text: Wow just amazing pizza and one of the best I’ve ever eaten! The bee sting was amazing and so was their famous original. The atmosphere is eclectic and definitely funky and strange but it’s an amazing experience and the food is so good I can eat this every day and not get tired of it!!!

author: Benito Camesta
review_text: Such a cool vibe, it's a bar with amazing pizza. I got the bee sting based on all the reviews and it doesn't disappoint. The dough is so light, there is a spicy to it but all the flavors compliment each other so well.

author: Amanda Lynch-Smith
review_text:
I’ve been to Roberta’s a bunch of times and it never disappoints, but I want to give a special shoutout to the staff who always make the experience memorable. I ordered the pizza with ricotta, white sauce, and added mushrooms (delicious), and even though there was a delay with it coming out, Simone went above and beyond. She was so attentive, kind, and genuinely fun to talk to — she really made me feel special.

Also huge thanks to Blair, who has helped me and my boyfriend out on Valentine’s Day and other visits to snag a table. Between the incredible food and the amazing team, Roberta’s is one of those places you always want to come back to.

author: Jose Miguel
review_text:
Funky spot with an amazing vibe and seriously good pizza!
The Bee Sting was hands down my favorite – spicy, sweet, perfectly balanced. We also tried the Lil Stinky, and it was packed with flavor.

Surprisingly, the salad blew me away. I’m not even a salad person, but this one was super flavorful and creative – a total standout.

The place has that refined grit – it doesn’t look fancy, but everything’s done with care and intention. That contrast between raw and elevated? It just works.

Definitely coming back!!!

author: Eric Lam
review_text:
Had a grown-up pizza party birthday dinner here. I haven't been back here for years, and everything's as good as I remembered.
We sat in the room in the back. I really liked the shipping container decor. Service was pretty good. Food came out quickly. Although we had a small issue with two of the pastas being way too salty, the rest of the food was excellent. The English Pea caramelle was nice. I particularly enjoyed their Margherita and Lupetto pizzas. I would also recommend their maitake mushrooms as well.

author: Diana Arday
review_text: The pizza here was 10/10. Really nice and freshly made. Only issue was they had 1 working restroom so the queue was long but other than that, a really nice place to eat and catch up with friends.

author: Adrien Qi
review_text: fire vibes inside but ordered takeout. satisfying chewy crust and very good flavors. texture couldve been better but we got takeout and ate after 20-15 min of walking

author: S Yoon
review_text: I'd describe the pies here as modern Neapolitan. These have a bit more structure than traditional Neapolitan pies. That said, the ingredients are fun and the vibe is cool. It's been a few years, but I'd definitely go back.

author: Ruben
review_text: I live in the neighborhood I’ve been here 3x and every time the staff was in a hurry and a bit rude (being annoyed when they didn’t hear something or not wanting to explain something on the menu etc). I understand that these simple customer service things don’t come naturally to people that don’t get paid a living wage, but Roberta’s is very group-oriented with tables (I don’t think they let you order just a slice 🤷🏻‍♂️) and that’s just the kind of thing that happens when dining as a group so I think the staff should be patient when someone has a question. So far I haven’t felt any kindness from the servers so I won’t be returning anytime soon. It’s also way overpriced, there’s way better pizza and cheaper cocktails right nearby. Go to Moondog for cocktails and to Starrlight for a full-size pizza

author: Patrick Zajac
review_text:
First time trying Ethiopian food and I’m glad it was at Bunna Cafe because this place was stellar! Absolutely loved the ambiance, service, and most importantly the food.

They start you off with a free plate of popcorn to snack on while you wait for your food which was so fun. Also, I happened to be in during their weekend Bunna Coffee Ceremony so I had a complimentary cup of the Bunna. It was very strong, spiced, and rich, with a prominent ginger undertone. Adding in the brown sugar cubes opened up the flavor so much. Delicious!

I tried the Lentil Sambusas which were super crispy. The filling inside was fine but adding on that cilantro lime sauce really tied it all together! There was a subtle spice too that I enjoyed.

For my main I went with the Beyaynetu Meal which was the 5 scoop option. I kinda wanted to go for the 7 scoop Feast to try more things but I’m glad I didn’t because the 5 scoop was very sizable for one person! I tried the Enguday Tibs, Shiro, Misis Wot, Yater Kik Alicha, and the seasonal option which was an Eggplant and Walnut Deberjan. WOW!!! Everything was so insanely flavorful and worked well with each other. I think my two favorites were the Shiro and the Yater Kik Alicha. Soooooo so so good I could eat a whole bowl of just those.

author: jen k
review_text: This was my first Ethiopian cuisine experience and I loved that they don't give you utensils for the full effect! The food isnt really a looker if you're not into pureed food, but the taste was delightful! Highly recommend and for any vegans or vegetarians craving some hearty food. I have gone 2 times now and they are just as good! The interaction (bread) they have is tangy and slightly sour.

author: Maitri Bhandari
review_text:
From the moment I stepped into Bunna Cafe, I was completely charmed. Tucked away in Brooklyn, this all-vegan Ethiopian spot radiates warmth and culture, and an inviting, communal vibe. They even host an authentic Ethiopian coffee ceremony in the evenings, which adds to the immersive feel.

The staff was wonderful, warm, welcoming, and happy to answer questions about the menu and traditions. We kicked off our meal with Kategna, a crispy, toasty injera snack paired with Daata, a spicy side sauce that delivered just the right amount of heat. Simple, but incredibly satisfying.

Next came the highlight: the Feast. It’s a platter of injera topped with vibrant scoops of various stews and vegetables. Each one was distinct, bursting with flavors. The crimini mushrooms were earthy and umami-rich, the lentils hearty and beautifully spiced, and the collard greens brought a fresh, slightly tangy contrast. The Shiro, a spiced chickpea stew, was deeply comforting and packed with flavors. Honestly, it was impossible to pick a favorite.
Every bite felt thoughtful, nourishing, and made to be shared. I sipped on refreshing Hibiscus tea throughout the meal, which was the perfect complement to the bold, warming flavors.

Bunna Cafe is a celebration of Ethiopian cuisine and culture. Fun, flavorful, communal, and deeply satisfying. I’ll definitely be coming back.

author: Ellen Levitt
review_text: I have gone here occasionally over the past several years and the food is always wonderful. I went today for lunch because it's Sigd and I wanted vegan food. The kale was amazing. The others really tasty too.

author: Siena WD
review_text:
Unfortunate that I finally found a go-to/favorite Ethiopian place in the city a few weeks before going home for the summer. It took some time to get here but I was very committed to procrastinating my homework, and if you're an ethiopian restaurant offering me a vegetarian combo there's really no limit to how far I'll travel for that. I got the feast for two (though I am only one. Next night dinner. It's called being smart) and apparently they offer this to go in a pizza box which is very smart and fun however I worried it would be clunky for the subway so instead I got a million containers of greatness. My photographs as always are of dubious quality, but rest assured the food was not.

The injera, thank god again, was sour, I hate when it's bland but this was far from it, the perfect vessel for all of everything. I don't know all the names of the dishes but I loved everything I ate. The mushrooms stood out, I love gomen, the split peas and red lentils were doing their thing, something was spicy and idk what it was but it was ASTOUNDING I say really the whole meal I was just thrilled with so I had it again that weekend and loved it just as much. When I picked up my orders both times! The person working was friendly and warm and unbelievably kind, I'll have to dine in next time because I imagine the service is top notch. I'm going to enjoy my summer away from the easy coast but I will say, this spot will be on my mind and I'm looking forward to being reunited with the greatness that is Bunna Cafe.

author: N. Sergew
review_text: Phenomenal place! Ver tasty vegan Ethiopian dishes, along with delicious coffee and spicy tea. Wonderful and attentive service. Went for brunch and the live DJ just enhanced the whole experience so much! Highly recommend!

author: Christopher Kong
review_text:
I had some business in the area and want something to eat and thought about Bunna! I had no reservations and had about a 20-30 minute wait on a Saturday night.

I am now convinced this is the BEST Ethiopian place for great vegetarian food! The place was packed even as late as I arrived. Very warm and accommodating staff.

The food was so on point! We ordered drinks as well and just as amazing as the food!

It is a little out of my normal area but I will surely go out of my way to get back here again.

author: Neha Rege
review_text:
Bunna Cafe was my first Ethiopian food experience, and it instantly made me fall in love with the cuisine.

The food was rich and flavorful, the ambience felt warm and authentic, and the service was friendly and attentive. A great spot for anyone trying Ethiopian food for the first time or looking for an authentic Ethiopian experience in Brooklyn.

author: Nicole Smith
review_text: Come here for brunch!!! The food was absolutely bonkers! Portions were also great for the price, two of us split three dishes and both had leftovers to take. Both of us really enjoyed our teas as well. The service was quick and kind and the vibes were wonderful with the music in the background. Highly recommend!

author: Jasmin
review_text: Best Ethiopian food in the city (that I know of). Flavorful and fully vegan!, value for money, and service is friendly and quick. Ambience is casual and cozy. Good playlist, on weekends they sometimes even have live music. Fri, Sat, and Sun they have the coffee ceremony at 5pm and serve free Ethiopian coffee, which is also delicious! Have been here for dinner multiple times and weekend brunch (different menu).

author: Laura
review_text: My mother and I had a lovely dinner at Bunna Cafe. The staff was attentive, kind, and courteous. Every bite of their food was a delight and the wine and tea were also delicious. The lighting and atmosphere were soothing. We were visiting the neighborhood for the day and would love to dine there again if we're in the area.

author: C. Tapia
review_text:
I came where with my parents who are VERY picky eaters but they loved the food!
The flavors are fantastic. The colorful portions are beautiful.

We had a handful of the lentil sambusas, the feast for two, their Ethiopian version of a Bellini (YUM) and the baklava for dessert.

A delicious meal with hearty portions. We left feeling satisfied but not overly stuffed.

And everything is so healthy and simple ingredients

author: Gary Gao
review_text: Great vegan food with wide variety and also good coffee. Personally I liked the samosas the most

author: Shako Liu
review_text: I’m a visual person and I love how colorful the foods are. But more than just visuals, the taste is supreme! I come here a lot when I crave for something delicious and healthy. The staff is always kind and friendly. This restaurant is a neighborhood gem!

author: Kelly He
review_text:
first time having ethiopian food! i think it tasted good and felt good quality but

1. didnt realize its vegetarian lol thats on me
2. the tables/chairs were weird heights so it was a little uncomfy and the live music on wednesdays was wayy too loud ://

we got the feast for 2 and feast for 3 for 5 of us. it was so big (see photos for size comparison) and the shai tea was p good too!

overall the food is good. id imagine youd love it if you were vegetarian and/or love ethiopian food but im not convinced its for me quite yet

author: Olivia Celice
review_text: I observed the consistency that builds Bunna Cafe's reputation. Worker attention was truly exceptional! The portions here are notably generous. The food works well, but the atmosphere truly excels. Hope this place impresses you too.

author: Queeny Qiu
review_text: Loved the ambiance of the restaurant! Lots of seating and great service. Didn’t know what to expect for vegan Ethiopian food but was not disappointed. The flavors were amazing and really enjoyed the roti that we got with our main dishes. Brunch prices were reasonable and portions were generous! Highly recommend!

author: Kiariladyboss
review_text:
First time trying Ethiopian food 🇪🇹 and i went with a friend for my b.day. Enjoyed the experience to eat on the same plate. We ordered the feast for 2 (even though that’s food for at least 3 people😂) for $49 + a couple of appetizer and mango juice (freshly squeezed) that is served with pomegranade syrup (if i am not mistaken).

On a mission to try all the vegan spots in NYC

author: Mo Da Prophet
review_text:
First time trying Ethiopian food? Go here!

Food:
Authentic and delicious food. Feast for 2 was perfect amount for 2 people. Each dish had its own distinct flavor and you can explore different flavor combos. Food came super fast as well.

Service:
Staff is friendly. They more less leave you alone. Perfect, if you’re looking to eat alone and not be bothered.

author: Floz Panseri
review_text:
Bunna is always the best.
On point from the time you walk in trough the ambience till the first bite.
I LOVE BUNNA. One of the best vegan worldwide

author: rachel
review_text:
Ayat, can only be described as a euphoric dining experience. This restaurant has quickly become a favorite among friends in the city. The atmosphere is incomparable, cozy enough for conversation but busy enough to hear the laughter and joy around you. The food is indescribable, beautifully seasoned with unforgettable flavor. The staff is also incredibly kind, and very thoughtful in their service.

Some menu highlights were the halloumi watermelon salad (truly life changing), the Pistachio Paradise Pizza, and the Chicken Shawarma. All dishes were amazing, but these were each unforgettable. Ayat is the spot to go if you want a unique and outstanding experience in a homey environment with beautiful ambiance. This is a must-try restaurant, I’ll be taking every visitor I have!

author: ana
review_text:
I had such a wonderful experience at Ayat! The food was absolutely delicious — full of flavor, fresh, and beautifully presented. The atmosphere was cozy and welcoming, perfect for both a casual night out or a special dinner.

Our server, Yulisa, made the experience even better. She was so attentive, kind, and knowledgeable about the menu. She made great recommendations and checked in at just the right moments without ever feeling rushed. You can tell she really cares about her guests having a great time.

I’ll definitely be coming back soon — everything from the service to the food was amazing!

author: Benjamin Freeberg
review_text: Pretty nice experience overall. Very warm and welcoming inside. The staff is a little standoffish they didn't make any conversation which was off-putting but my friend and I had a good time together. BYOB is nice too. I'll definitely come back to try more of the food.

author: Rachel Cheung
review_text: I’m very picky in a way that I know enough about ingredients and cooking techniques so  believe me when I give them a rare 5 stars from me. Top quality ingredients, hummus was silky smooth you can taste every subtle flavors because they use good chickpeas, spice, and olive oil. Then the mixed grilled platter with lamb chop/ kebab were outstanding. Juice clean fat and well cooked.  Desserts are pretty but too sweet in my opinion. Wonderful service our Ecuadorian waiter was excellent!

author: Kenia Mendez
review_text:
The service from Lissette was excellent – very kind and attentive the whole time. The food was delicious and different, full of flavor and beautifully served. I loved the pita bread, so soft and fresh. I tried the Hibiscus Margarita (the purple drink with mint) and it was amazing, super refreshing and unique. My dish was the Mixed Platter, a perfect combination of chicken, lamb, yellow rice, and veggies – everything was spectacular!

Definitely an experience worth repeating. 💚

author: Deval Shah
review_text: Amazing food . Everything we tried ( and we tried many vegetarian items) was very high quality ingredient wise and also well cooked. This place is now my #1 for Mediterranean style food. great addition to the community. Thank you for your effort! The pita, fried halloumi, muhamarra, kanafe, eggplant, labneh, vegan platter were all amazing.

author: MOE JARADAT
review_text:
What an unfortunate situation — this restaurant was on my bucket list. Unfortunately, the experience was spoiled by the less-than-professional behavior of Natalia.
That said, the restaurant itself tells a wonderful story, backed by an amazing menu. The atmosphere truly reflects and supports the spirit of the people of the land.
Special thanks to Susan, who made things better for us.
Constructive note: Please avoid serving Arabic coffee in a glass tea cup — you know the culture better than that

author: Amirah Randolph
review_text: I absolutely loved dining here. The cuisine was delectable. The staff were lovely, especially Suzan. The live music tied everything together. This was the perfect birthday experience. I would definitely recommend everyone come and visit.

author: Sunny Patel
review_text:
Place is gorgeous! Food was alright. Service was alright as well.

Don’t get the spicy chicken kebabs - subpar at best! The chicken sumac dish was good - very mild taste thou.

I’d go back to try other dishes. Didn’t love what I had.

The pita and hummus was great thou!

author: Jacob Moss
review_text: Honestly everything was phenomenal. We got the Mezze Filistini, the Makloubeh platter, the Watermelon Haloumi salad, roasted cauliflower, and the Baklava Sundae. All the dips in the Mezze were stunning—best tabouleh I’ve ever had. And a huge shoutout to that watermelon haloumi salad, it was revelatory. Like, I didn’t know food could taste like that. Really nice atmosphere, overlooking the park with open concept, and also it was a Saturday and they had live music!

author: Shonalya Fonseka
review_text: Amazing food, amazing atmosphere truly one of the best restaurants in the city. Staff was so kind and helpful especially Chris, the art was so beautiful and you’ll see only smiles on everyone’s face. The energy was great definitely excited to come back again

author: Jack Michalski
review_text: Went for a birthday dinner. Service was accommodating and friendly. It was BYOB and we brought a bottle of wine and there was no corking fee. Food was good across the board. Lots of vegetarian/vegan options. We got: baba ghanoush (smokey), fried halloumi, vegan platter (too many good things to list but especially liked the zahir and wara dawali), and the grilled salmon salad. Reasonable prices. Will definitely come back again

author: Ss Kk
review_text: We celebrated our friend’s birthday here and had such an amazing time! The food was delicious, the drinks were on point, and the place has such a great vibe. Definitely recommend checking it out. Special shoutout to our waitress Suzan she was the sweetest and made the night even better. Thank you for the great service!

author: Nick Richards
review_text:
This spot is always a 10/10. Informed and educated waiters and staff, delicious food with huge portions, and it’s BYOB!

They also have different atmospheres, outside, inside, and downstairs - each with their own vibe.

author: Sapphira Bella
review_text: We came here for a friend’s birthday dinner a few weeks ago and got the downstairs seating section. The place was jam packed and very busy. It’s BYOB so we brought our own wine, tequila, etc. The vibe was cute and homey. We had the appetizers to start with of za’atar, labneh, hummus, etc. The bread was not great quality and the dips were OK. We tried the vegetable platter, a lamb kebab and a chicken kebab. Everything came with pilaf and salad. Overall the food was very OK. It was decent, lacked seasoning and some of it was not cooked well. The service was very good and they accommodated our large party but the food was underwhelming.

author: Astrid
review_text: Ayat, where to begin? Sometimes a place draws you in because of its reputation. Ayat was one of those places. Seated on a Sunday, I came in with moderate expectations of a thorough menu dedicated to showcasing Palestinian cuisine. I was not disappointed. From the zaatar to the olives in olive oil, to the heaping mounds of sizzling chicken shawarma, Ayat is a place that beats expectations. Nearly too much food to eat, so go with friends that like to share and indulge to your hearts desire. Food is the star, but the service is excellent too, and the ambience is deeply inviting. Palestinian to its core - what a beautiful place!

author: Kee Diamond
review_text: I went to a Palestinian restaurant in New York for the first time. As expected from its popularity, everything was delicious. I was very satisfied with both the atmosphere and the service. I definitely want to go again

author: Daniella Favila
review_text: Good was amazing! Liz, our server, was the most kind and tentative server! The food was very warm and comforting, we loved the BYOB aspect and the people were amazing and kind! They knew how to explain the dishes well and were personable.

author: Arin Dutta
review_text:
Bushwick branch of the Ayat Palestinian restaurant network in the NYC region. Was pretty crowded already on an early Friday evening. The location also opens a small patio facing the Maria Hernandez Park so you may want to target that.

Food:
- at this location at least, not that amazing. Pita is flaky and thin, and nicely flavored. You can have better in the 5 boroughs area, sure.
- hummus: my dinner companion is bit of an expert and according to her (I concur), it was heavy on the tahini and lacked bite (traditional Palestinian hummus can be a bit creamier than other Levantine recipes so this may well be true to design). It is nicely presented in a traditional earthenware bowl, as is most of the food.
- Shawarma platter : we got the mixed grill version. The rice and toppings were generous and the meat was flavored though not excessively
- Fattoush: nice and lemony, with a good helping of fried pita chips
- We asked for kibbeh, and only after 15 minutes of waiting, were told that they had none!

Overall: not the best nor the worst Palestinian food you’ll have in the region. Service is a bit klutzy.

Ordering tip: the shawarma platter is pretty large. Can satisfy two people (with a starter like hummus) if you are not ravenous.

Photo of mixed shawarma platter, hummus, and fattoush attached

author: Denissa Gonzalez
review_text:
We received complimentary pita bread fresh out of the oven such a nice touch! The hummus was delicious as an appetizer, and the lentil soup might honestly be the best I’ve ever had. I also really appreciated that they don’t go heavy on the salt, but my cucumber and tomato salad ended up way under seasoned  it definitely needed a pinch more.

As for the service, our waitress seemed kind but very out of it. She looked tired and sad, like her body was present but her mind was elsewhere. She kept forgetting things, tripped over her feet a few times, and even dropped the dressing. Service felt a bit off, but I genuinely hope she’s okay. It left me a little concerned.

author: Dwight Kenneth
review_text:
I really wanted to like Salty Lunch Lady, but I honestly don’t get the hype.

The sandwiches are small, slow to come out, and expensive, ranging from about $14–$18, and there’s nothing about them that feels special. The ingredients might be good quality, but the execution is very basic. We tried the chicken sandwich and the turkey sandwich and both were just okay. Nothing memorable. The seeded sesame bun didn’t taste very fresh either, which is a big miss for a sandwich spot.

The service setup is also strange. You have to grab your own sandwich, your own utensils, and then bus your own plates and cups afterward. For those prices, that feels off. It’s not a casual deli price point, but it’s a self-service experience.

I will say, the desserts are excellent. The ginger cake was moist and the cream was delicious. But $12 for a single slice of cake is outrageous, even factoring in overhead. It just feels disconnected from reality.

Overall, this place feels overhyped. I don’t understand the glowing reviews. In my opinion, they need to either make the sandwiches bigger and better seasoned, lower the prices, or lean fully into the baked goods and rethink the pricing and service model. Even something as simple as having staff clear tables would improve the experience.

As it stands, I wouldn’t rush back.

author: Kary Sartan
review_text: Too many good things to say about this place not even an exaggeration one of the best sandwiches I’ve ever had in my entire life and the brass monkey what a cute and fun drink, kind of like a bootleg mimosa, but even better! Great for the neighborhood I will definitely be back. I want to try every single sandwich on the menu and all of you should too.

author: Brett East
review_text:
These are great sandwiches. It’s a seat yourself kind of place, so snag a table and then line up to order.

We had some tres leches cake, the Chicky sandwich and the Fancy Bologna sandwich

author: Yagazie Emezi
review_text: My friend had spoken highly of this place to check out, however, we were disappointed. At first glance, it’s a cute space. Upon closer look, the cushions to sit on were absolutely filthy, didn’t feel comfortable sitting in my shorts. Table areas also weren’t cleaned off from previous guests. And the sandwiches were simply just okay.

author: chris caracciolo
review_text:
I'm only sorry that I haven't gotten here sooner.
This is one of those places that's a real
Feel Good Spot.
Everything here makes you feel warm and comfortable.  Simply put together to make you feel welcome . The food here  is over the top Delicious.
Every Bite.  if it's sweet or savory, you're in for a real treat .
Absolutely the Very Best Chocolate Pudding Pie I've ever had.
Dreamy and delicious.
The tuna melt was nothing like I've had before . Light, tasty,flavourful, great bread,incredible cheese, and just
So well put together.
I really wish Chef and her team a great Big thanks for making it a great experience.
If you haven't stopped in, treat yourself to a great  lunch .
Don't wait as long as I did .....

author: Omar Mrani
review_text:
The dill party didn't completely live up to the hype, but was still a good sandwich! Prices are certainly steep for what you get, but that's par for the course in the city.

Still recommend folks try this place out! Great atmosphere and friendly faces, and the desserts are hard to resist

author: Blake Rasmussen
review_text: This is a nice little deli with very good sandwiches. The prices are steep, but the sandwiches are excellent and very clearly in demand. It’s on the NY Times’ top 100 list, and at least one of the sandwiches, the dill party, I rated very highly. I don’t quite think this cracks the top sandwiches for me but I’d happily come back - the sandwiches are relatively small, no sides, but very tasty. We arrived at open, and admitted the kitchen was swamped. It took over 30 minutes just to get a slice of cake, and 20 minutes+ for sandwiches. That said, I’m sure there are less busy times of the day and if you manage to get in when there isn’t a rush, the food is really excellent - particularly the desserts!

author: Saddmun Ahsan
review_text:
If coming on the weekend be prepared for a WAIT. However, the sandwiches are worth it.

Came on Sunday afternoon at 12:30p and it was packed. Like a line out the door kind of packed. But it moves relatively quickly. However, after we got through the line it did take 45 min for us to get our two sandwiches.

The sandwiches were delicious though. We got the dill party and the chicky, both were delicious. I personally liked the dill party a bit better as it was heavy on the dill (mayo, pickles, + dill havarti) with fresh turkey (they brine and roast in-house) - a delicious combo.

The chicky was good, I just found it a bit hard to eat with the harder seeded bun and slippery so the insides would just fall out unfortunately. Also the sandwich itself was a tad too salty (and I eat a lot of salt) - but that was probably due to the feta

Overall, a great sandwich spot that's a must try if in the area!

ALSO DESSERTS! Which sell out super quick so get whatever they have!

author: Siena WD
review_text:
Simple things done exceptionally well. Finally made the trek for an Easter slice of coconut cake (threw in a pie last minute. It just looked so good, and when I figured I could either have it or not have it the decision sort of made itself). Hour on the subway was well worth it. The neighborhood was really nice, lotta charm, good people, and the trend continued- inside the luncheonette was BEAUTIFUL. They've done a great job with the space, the teal paint, tile, flowers on the hanging lights, you can tell it was all done with a lot of thought and a lot of love including of course! The food. I could see their sandwiches getting made through the SANDWICH WINDOW and they looked incredible. I will be storming back for some tuna.

The desserts were fantastic. The cake was fluffy, buttery buttercream, and not too sweet! Would not have minded more coconut flavor in the cake itself, you can just never have enough. The lemon curd in the middle was perfect. Actually it went very well with the orange curd pie which was my favorite of the two, the orange filling was so bright and sharp and the cookie crust had this great salt to it, fresh zest on top, it all just tasted GOOD, like they use quality ingredients. Just overall good vibes. My order was ready early, the person behind the counter was delightful. Great food, happy people. What else is there?

author: Jennifer Lu
review_text:
How good could a corner sandwich shop be? Extremely good.

Possibly my #1 Tuna Melt by far. The tuna is generously mixed with pickles and mayo, along with the gooey cheese makes every bite a true delight. Sourdough bread was super light, toasted to perfection, crunchy and airy. Just wonderful.

author: Hector Berrios
review_text:
Salty Lunch Lady’s sandwiches were truly delectable. I have the tuna melt simply delicious. Bread nicely toasted cheese melted just write and the correct amount of tuna made the sandwich perfect for my tasting. The gooey gratin simply out of this world!! The fresh squeezed lemon added a touch that simply married all the flavors together. (Psss you might want another!! lol) The spicy culi was a nicely “Italined” the meats alongside the provolone and chili mayo was again perfectly married. Thank you for the delicious experience. ( The plating made me feel like mom just served my meal with LOVE!!)

Well Done! #SALTYNESS@itsfinest!!!
Solid 5⭐️

author: Kayla Morin
review_text:
Delicious sandwiches—we had the cauliflower and leek and butternut squash.  The butternut squash sandwich was packed full of greens, soft squash, and a ricotta/goat cheese mix with a lemony-pesto sauce.  Incredible flavors I had never tried before.  The cauliflower/leek sandwich was made with focaccia and was filled with warm, gooey Gruyère among other cheeses.  Cute, homey atmosphere with lots of seating. We arrived at opening on a Sunday with a line already out the door, which was expected—not docking a star for the line.

Giving 4 stars instead of 5 because it took almost 30 minutes to get our sandwiches (after waiting in line) and the sandwiches were a little small for the price.

Overall highly recommend!  Great options for vegetarians like myself.

author: Coach A. Taylor
review_text: That Gooey Gratin Sandwich 🤯 Lawd Have Mercy! The Cauliflower + Leek Gratin Sandwich with Cheddar & Gruyere is incredible – cheesy, crunchy, and the lemon drizzle is a game-changer. Fried chicken sandwich? Perfect. Coffee Cake Layer Cake? Grandma-level good. Cozy vibes, amazing food. Highly recommend! @greedygirlsclub

author: Anna Lee
review_text:
Update: Had such a heartwarming delivery experience today. I ordered sandwiches and cakes for delivery and the order arrived without the cakes. Dria called me a couple times and was very apologetic and while I was fine with just a refund, they said they were still holding the cakes for me if I could just place another delivery order for them. The cakes were delivered, satisfied my craving, and I was fully comped for the mistake. I’ve never had a business go so above and beyond for a delivery order. Thanks so much!

—
Such a cute space, friendly service, and the cherry pistachio layer cake was insane. Dill Party was also yummy.

author: Mia Huynh
review_text:
My friend saw this spot on social media and wanted to try it, so we both headed out here to check out this luncheonette for lunch! The interior of the restaurant is cute and quaint and there are small tables for you to enjoy your sandwiches at. Service was good and took about 20-30 minutes for our sandwiches to be made.

They only have a couple items on their menu and unfortunately the one that my friends wanted (the dill) was already sold out. However, we did get a couple others: the brocollini, tuna, ham & cheese, and their chicky. Everything was great and the portions were huge. Cute spot, but (imo) nothing crazy. I would only come back if I was in the area.

author: Noah Scott
review_text: Run don’t walk to get the tomato sandwich while it’s in season. I like to add their house brined and roasted turkey. Out of tomato season the tuna crunch hits every time. Every sandwich crafted with care. Love me some Salty’s

author: Illiana Gallardo
review_text:
Pies are good, but the service was rude and from what I’ve heard from neighbors, also super slow. I went a couple of Sundays ago, excited to try it since I grew up in the area and like supporting small, growing businesses. Unfortunately, I won’t be back or recommend it.

The girl at the front was rude and acted like she was doing us a favor. I asked what the desserts of the day were, and she replied unkindly, “We always have a cookie, cake, and pie.” No follow-up description, no menu to reference, so we chose the pie, I guess. She didn’t say anything else, which left me unsure whether she had even processed the order until I saw the price pop up on the screen.

My friend ordered next. The employee placed a box in front of her without saying a word. My friend had to ask if it was hers, and the girl said “yes” as if it should have been obvious. If someone hates customer service, maybe don’t have them customer-facing.

I think feedback is a friend, so here it is: for a new business in a changing neighborhood, kindness and respect toward customers should be a priority.

author: Zoey Tang
review_text:
Yum, everything was delicious. Self-service.
I think the restaurant layout can be a little more efficient, people seemed to keep running into other people...

Note: while everything was really delicious, the food was not cheap at all, I somehow spent $40 with no alcohol!

author: Cat C
review_text:
We waited in line and ordered two sandwiches to go at 130pm. The young lady told us it'll take 30 min to make so we asked if we can leave and come back. She said yes and that our sandwiches will probably be up front so we can just ask for them. We come back at 210pm and asked about our sandwiches. A guy went to the back to check. While he was back there, the young lady came back to the register and we asked her if she put our name on our previous order. She said yes and also went back to check. She came back and didn't say anything to us so we assumed they just put it in at that time. No one said anything to us or apologized. It's now an hour later and still no food. The guy approached us and said our order is almost ready. We sat down next to someone who also waited an hour and complained about the service. The guy offered us a free cookie for the wait. We finally got our order and ate them at home. They were okay, definitely not worth the 1+ hour wait. We also got a slice of the PB&J cake. That was pretty delicious. One star for that.

Overall, the young lady's vibe at the counter we didn't care for. She didn't care that our food wasn't made nor did she tell us anything about it. The guy was nicer and more empathetic.

author: Georgina Arroyo
review_text:
I had been wanting to go here foreverrrr and I guess it’s partially my mistake for finally coming on a Sunday. But the wait was very very long. We were told 30 minutes, but we waited an hour for two sandwiches. Sandwiches that are pretty pricey. 2 sammys with no drinks or chips or treats were over $30. Now… my sandwhich was amazing. Truly truly delicious. But there’s very little I will spend that much on and wait so long for- especially in that chaotic small space. There’s no table service, which on a busy Sunday really sucks because everyone is standing around trying to pounce on the next available table.
So, if you do come here, I would try during the week. I’m assuming it’s a bit more calm then. This definitely won’t become a regular spot for me, but it’s tasty and I’m sure I’ll visit again at some point.

author: Sunu M
review_text:
My best friend and I have been frequenting Rolos since we watched that one video about how their lasagna is made. It's been a special treat when we can manage to get a table (one that's well worth the wait).

The staff here is truly incredible. A lot of restaurants in the city can be condescending and rude, but the entire staff at Rolos is beyond kind and accommodating.

If you're able to snag a res, which we were today, you're in for a real treat. When I put in the res notes that this would be our last dinner together given my leaving NYC, the staff made it truly special!

Standout dishes: chili polenta bread, cheeseburger, skirt steak, and of course, the lasagna!

While we went back and forth about where to have our "last supper" as our server called it, we knew Rolo's was the only right choice. The food is always consistent, outstanding, and a memorable experience.

I couldn't have imagined a better way to close out my NY days. Thank you so much to the Rolos staff for such a considerate, caring, and extraordinary experience.

author: Queen Dimples
review_text: Made reservations walked in and was pleasantly surprised..this is a busy establishment reservations are recommended..Natalie who was our waitress was an absolute doll. So informative with a wealth of knowledge about the food. The food hands down was a ten out of ten. We ordered the crispy potatoes for the table, yum and yum. A second order was made immediately don't judge. I ordered the eggs with the polenta bread sooo good.my friend ordered the French toast which was to die for..need I say more. The food is very filling and so very delicious.

author: XT
review_text:
My first time here, I got the burger after hearing the hype. The waiter made it a point to mention that it was still available (because they’ll run out later in the day) and asked if we wanted to reserve one. I was thinking it would be the best thing on the menu but it really was just okay. I’m glad I tried it, but I kind of regretted getting it. It also made me suspicious of all the other things on the menu that I didn’t get to try.

I went back recently to give some other things a try and I’m really really happy I did. Everything hit this time. The polenta bread, the lasagna, the leafy green salad, and maggie’s little pumpkin. I’d give them all 5 Stars.

If you save room for dessert, get the brown butter apple tart. You won’t regret it.

In terms of service and atmosphere, they were great both times. Super friendly and very ridgewood, so you can come and expect to feel at home.

author: Rezaul Khan
review_text:
The house dry-aged steak was really good, like one of the top five steaks I have had. Side dishes were a bit too salty for me, especially the greens. Calabrian chili butter polenta bread was also delicious.
Strawberry almond tart was just okay. Service was excellent. Casual ambiance. I would go back.

author: Christine
review_text: This is a festive vibrant restaurant with good vibe and excellent service. It is actually quite large once you walked into the restaurant and passed the hallway and then the cool open kitchen. We had the chili bread, crudo, wagyu steak, green lasagna, grilled pork, crispy potatoes, wine and desserts.  They were all delicious especially the bread, steak and pork.  Yummy to the tummy 🤗

author: Jake G
review_text: Posting this review without reading other comments.  I am not influenced by others.  The food was amazing!  The two layer lasagna was delicious. The crispy potatoes were delicious. The bread was delicious.  The service was quick, kind and accommodating.  Make it a must try.

author: James Geigel
review_text: For the first time , it was amazing. However, usually, when it's dinner time, I expect it to be a bit more calming and quiet. But overall, great things were done the food. The service was top tier, making sure that everyone got their meal at the same time. So a lot of good work was put into it. It is worth bringing a loved one and a family to enjoy. Now, there can be some areas of improvement. The peach dessert could have been in a wider vessel with a smaller spoon because I brought a friend who was blind trying to get the dessert from the cup, and the pepper from the burger special could be chopped than leaving it whole.

author: Peyton Marshak
review_text: This was one of the best dinners that I have had in awhile. Rolo’s really does such an after a job at creating an atmosphere that feels both like home and fine dining. Everything on the menu catches your eye, but I much say that sitting by the oven you can easily tell what is the most popular item is: the lasagna. Undoubtedly one of the best bites of pasta in the city, and I will also add that their burger can stand with many of the other high caliber bistro’s in town. Such a delight, I would easily recommend Rolo’s to all of my friends and family. I can’t wait to go back already!

author: Amandip Kaur
review_text: Charming ambiance and good place for group dinner. This place is super famous for the 2 sheet lasagna but personally I was not a fan, instead I found the ricotta cavatelli pasta to be the star on the menu — also loved the almond tart (aromatic and nicely presented). Skip the skirt steak (prime cut is better) and polenta bread with calabrion chili (take sesame & wild oregano instead). Very kind staff: Hunter was exceptional with service and made us feel very welcome !

author: Hyojung
review_text:
The bread here is really chewy, nutty, and full of flavor!
I highly recommend the different kinds of bread. The pasta and lasagna were also very tasty—the pasta itself was excellent, and the menu was unique yet delicious!
If you’re in Brooklyn, you should definitely visit. I recommend it.
The atmosphere is great too!

author: Naile Ruiz
review_text: Came here for brunch with friends. The burger had run out, but we ordered a variety of plates to try. The polenta bread was incredible and the French toast was perfectly sweet. The war fries were crunchy and salty but I would've preferred the sauce on the side. The vegetables were great and the whole meal felt like a perfect balance. The service and athomsphere were great, bustling with positive energy.

author: Sonya M. Sumner
review_text:
I’ve had Rolo’s on my list for a while, and it lived up to every bit of the hype. The space has a warm neighborhood feel but the food and service are truly next level! Everything we ordered was outstanding!

The wood fired polenta bread with Calabrian chili butter was a knockout. Soft, flavorful, with just the right amount of heat. The flavors from the wood fired oven gave it a subtle smokiness that made it really special.

The cheesy potato croquettes were divine, warm, gooey, and incredibly comforting. Think the best version of a mozzarella stick, but with potato and better cheese— who wouldn’t love this?!

The fluke crudo with carrot vinaigrette, serrano, and pumpkin seeds was bright and punchy, with pristine fish and beautifully balanced flavors. The fluke was great quality so it’s clear to see Rolo’s really cares about souring quality ingredients. The ricotta cavatelli with creamed corn, pecorino, and black pepper was another standout. The pasta had the perfect bite, and the sweet corn flavor was so pure and lovely that I kept going back for more.

We also had the two sheet lasagna verde bolognese (beef and pork). It was rich, hearty, and had that delicious wood fired taste. I found the salt a touch assertive, but my husband absolutely loved it and called it one of his favorite dishes of the night.

The crispy potatoes war style with their homemade sauce deserve their own applause. They might sound simple, but the combination of peanut sauce, onions, and kewpie mayo was unreal. The fry on those potatoes was perfect, and they even stayed crispy when we reheated them the next day.

Dessert was bread pudding à la mode, solid but not my favorite of the night, which says more about how exceptional everything else was.

The spicy pineapple margaritas were phenomenal. Perfectly balanced, fruity, spicy, and not too sweet. I had three and would have happily had a fourth!

And the service? Flawless!!! Ask to sit in Atticus’ section and trust his recommendations completely. He was friendly, attentive, and clearly knows the menu inside out. I told him I wanted the dishes that truly impress, and he delivered on every single one. I love a nice person and he was truly very kind!

Rolo’s is the kind of restaurant that reminds you why you love dining out, with fantastic food, amazing drinks, and service that makes you feel taken care of. I can’t wait to go back!

author: Jing Jing Gong
review_text:
Amazingly cute place that’s surprisingly big. The staff was very nice, chill, and gave excellent recommendations. Burger is a must; tuna crudo was also delicious. Hunter was very helpful and made sure we had enough water without prompting.

We were too full for dessert this time but will definitely come back to try them next time!

author: Glenn C
review_text:
Side note- Was here back in mid May and the menu has slightly changed so the prices might be slightly different. In short, I recommend the small plates much more than the main dishes. Get the flatbread, stracciatella, crispy potatoes, and order the lasagna if you have to get a main.

Anyway, I was back at this spot a few months ago with a small group for dinner having been here once prior. By comparison to our first meal, I would say this dinner was worse by comparison mostly due to the overcooked proteins while the small plates were excellent as well as the potatoes so it was a very uneven meal. The staff was friendly and there was enough room for us to sit comfortably. To drink, I had the "Martini Spanish" for $17 with Mahón gin, Atxa Blanco vermouth, sherry, olive brine, and pepper. The martini was unique being more vegetal/botanical forward with plenty of gin in particular and was an interesting sip throughout the evening.

We started with two of the small plates which happened to be the same plates I had a couple years ago. As per before, the Wood-Fired Polenta Flatbread for $13 with Calabrian chili butter was delicious with a perfectly charred bread. The chili butter is wonderful and while I still do not like paying for bread, this is a rare exception.

Again, the Stracciatella Cheese for the same price with silk chili and sumac was wonderful. The cheese was silky and the bit of sourness and bitterness from the combination of the chili and sumac worked perfectly. Honestly if I was to come back here again, I would make a meal out of these two things and maybe one other smaller plate or dessert.

This time, I got to try the Two-Sheet Lasagna for $32 which is served with verde bolognese which was the best entree by default. As someone who loves end pieces, the best thing about this lasagna was the texture with its mixture of crunch and softness. However, the bolognese itself was almost a bit too light with it lacking any richness and any type of meaty flavor so while the outside was nice, the inside was lacking. This was good but not as good as all the old hype surrounding it but was still the best of the large plates.

Also pretty good was the Wagyu Beef Skirt Steak for $48 which was decently portioned with a nice herb butter on top. The steak itself was cooked on the rarer end of medium rare so it had a bit too much of a chew unfortunately even for skirt steak. Outside of the chewiness, I would recommend it as if it was cooked well, the dish would have been excellent.

The Pork T-Bone for $35 with pine nuts and grilled spring onion agrodolce was also just OK. While the outside was nicely cooked, the inside of the pork wasn't super tender. The pine nuts added some nice crunch with the sweet onion mix added a nice extra flavor but overall, I found the dish both a bit chewy and too sweet.

Last of the entrees and certainly least was the Charred Half Chicken for $34 with salsa verde, mayo, and green tomatoes. The chicken had a nice outside sear but the meat itself wasn't too tender and I would honestly be pretty surprised if it was brined. The sauce had a bit too much sourness for my liking and this is coming from someone who loves a bit of sourness in their dishes which doesn't help either. I found the dish in other words unbalanced and overcooked and I wouldn't recommend it at all.

We also got the Crispy Potatoes "War Style" for $12 which is apparently a mix of spicy peanut sauce and kewpie mayo. I liked the texture of the potatoes with a mix of some crispier parts and softer ones. The only complaint I could make is that I wish there was more peanut sauce but overall, it was still very tasty.

At the price point for the entrees, it's harder to not judge this place more severely. While I liked or loved three dishes, the remaining three had major faults with the best entree (lasagna) being just OK. For wood-fired food, there's other spots I would recommend much more heavily such as the similarly hard to get into Theodora or if you can't get into the former, Peasant which just has better food for the price point.

author: Mark LoGiurato
review_text: The salad was inedible due to the amount of salt in it.  The polenta bread was good, but again over salted.  The better were oversalted as well.  The malfadine pasta was correctly salted.  The service at the bar was good as were the well drinks.

author: Joy Julius
review_text:
I got the wagyu steak salad medium rare. steak was perfectly cooked. however salad was just one vegetable it seems. got hints of bitterness through certain bites but it was balanced out by the lemon. overall great concept! Green juice was a surprising refresher, just had a tad too much ice.

The atmosphere was a constant flurry of loud music unfortunately so it seemed ppl talked louder to overcome that. I had a lunch for one and didn’t quite find that enjoyable because of it.

author: Joseph Bender
review_text: Delicious meal! Service was a bit spotty, and getting a table was a nightmare. But definitely one of the best spots in Ridgewood. Highly recommend the bread with stracciatella.

author: Elodie Sutter
review_text: Went to eat here today and did not have a pleasant food experience. We ordered some appetizers that were okay My husband ordered the lasagna and I ordered the steak. Let me just say the food had us questioning if we had Covid again because it did not taste or smell like anything. Very bland. The steak was served pretty much raw and we asked if we could be cooked longer to a medium rare/medium and the picture I have below is from the second time they gave it to us. Even the server asked “is that even better than before”. Honestly, just wanted to leave after this, and our server was very nice and accommodating and told us he would remove the steak off of our bill. Overall, very disappointed and I am not sure how this place has pretty high ratings considering our experience here. Please only come here with someone you don’t like.

author: dazz whatsup
